title: Traigent Best Config Repo Manifest v2
description: Index of best-config specs committed to a repository. Note this envelope had a version constant in the SDK (traigent.best_config_manifest.v1) but no schema anywhere - the shape was governed by one implementation's code. v2 governs it here and adds two things. First, every entry carries hash_algorithm, so a manifest written under one algorithm can never be verified under another: an entry whose algorithm a reader does not recognise is INVALID rather than upgradable, and the reader fails closed. Second, exported_at moves here from the spec's provenance. Export time is a fact about producing this manifest, not about the configuration, and keeping it inside the spec is what made an otherwise identical config hash differently on every export. A repo manifest is a user artifact under version control - not a reconstructible cache - so migration must back it up and regenerate it from its spec source rather than deleting it.

exported_at.description: When this manifest was written. Envelope metadata, deliberately outside any hashed spec.

configs.description: One entry per config_id. The key is the config_id; entries carry no config content, only the pointer and the digests needed to verify the spec file on load. Keys are constrained by propertyNames to the same config_id definition best_config_v2 uses, so a manifest can never index an entry under a key the config envelope itself would reject.

path.description: Spec filename relative to the manifest. A bare filename, never a traversing or absolute path.

hash_algorithm.description: Required per entry rather than once per manifest: entries are written independently over time, so a single envelope-level value would silently mislabel any entry written under a different algorithm.
